title: Horizon and Terminal
premise: Wendell Ravensworth discovers the impossible manifest lists his dead wife's name aboard a ship that never flew, and the cargo is a memory-recording that proves the war's opening strike was staged by both governments. Smuggling it means betraying every faction that has kept him alive for twenty years; destroying it means letting the lie stand. Pursued by customs enforcers and the memory's original courier — who turns out to be his wife, alive and erased — Wendell must choose between delivering the truth and keeping her. He delivers it, broadcasting the memory as his ship burns up in reentry, ending the war at the cost of everything he carried.
about_author: Ines Pemberton is a former orbital logistics analyst who turned to fiction after a decade of writing shipping manifests in low Earth orbit. She lives in a coastal town where she repairs radios and insists the future will smell like ozone and salt.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Was
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell. Running contraband through contested orbits, Wendell finds an unfamiliar name on a manifest for a ship decommissioned twenty years ago: Maren Ravensworth, his wife, listed as living crew. The emotional beat is vertigo — grief cracked open by bureaucratic error, and the first spark of dangerous hope that pulls him off his route.

chapters.title: Contraband Heart
chapters.summary: POV: Wendell, with interludes from customs officer Sefa Idris hunting him. Wendell traces the ghost manifest to a black-market memory vault and finds a recording proving the war's first strike was staged. The courier who hid it there was Maren — alive, her memories wiped. Rising tension: duty says surrender the evidence; love says find her first.

chapters.title: Terminal Velocity
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Wendell and Maren. Wendell reaches Maren, but restoring her memories may destroy her — the recording is fused to what remains of her mind. Enforcers close in; Sefa offers Wendell amnesty to hand it over. Climax: Maren chooses to remember, and together they decide the message must be broadcast from orbit, a one-way delivery run.

chapters.title: Horizon
chapters.summary: POV: Maren, then Wendell's final transmission. They burn toward the relay, pursued, broadcasting the staged-strike memory across every band as their ship breaks apart in reentry. Resolution: the war stalls, then ends; on the ground, strangers receive two names in the signal — a smuggler and his wife — remembered not as casualties but as couriers who finally delivered.
